neighbours.label: The Arabic 'and' (و) written as a separate word after a comma in a running list of three or more sheikhs (الشيخ + name, then ", و الشيخ" + name, repeated), strongest from the second 'و' on; the same list with other titles (doctor, prince, imam, professor), cities or books, two-item lists, or with 'و' glued to the next word stays weak. Separately and more weakly, it also fires on the indentation just before a bracket that closes a multi-line call or list in code.
neighbours.short: standalone Arabic 'و' continuing a list of sheikhs (+ code closing-bracket indent)
neighbours.notes: Step-in reader of bonsai1/L34/N3918- (drop 0.01, tiny: a late sparse pole feeds little into the last layer; this reader's label has nothing to do with hockey). Feeders first: L33/N9606- (space before inline code comment; its + pole is indentation before a closing bracket) and L22/N9377- (Arabic 'و' prefix) match the two triggers. Probes: sheikh lists 0.74-0.91; same frame with doctor/prince/professor/imam 0.10-0.26, cities/books 0.07-0.21, glued 'والشيخ' 0.16, two-item list 0.11. Code dedent before closing bracket 0.22-0.59 (solver leak). Blind test uses the Arabic comma '،'; probes mostly used ','. Test written blind by a second author from the label only.
